batch.identity: Plain Windows CMD HTTP command poller; no obfuscation.
batch.path: backward again label -> curl -fsS -o job.dat HTTPS -> set /p task=<job.dat -> %task% >result.log -> curl POST literal output=!task! -> timeout /t 10 -> goto again.
batch.verdict: Repeated unvalidated remote command execution with a fixed controller and no consent or authorization path supports a likely backdoor. Reserved .example host suggests an inert demonstration; neither a running deployment nor authorized administration was supplied.
batch.limits: The POST never reads result.log. Delayed expansion is not enabled here: !task! is literal unless inherited, in which case it sends the command text. No successful command/output transfer is claimed.
batch.hostile_coverage_goal: One distinct hostile behavior is supported and already covered by a byte-bound file/variable/backward-loop rule plus a hostile command-polling composite. Inspected all lines and CMD expansion semantics for persistence, payload staging beyond command retrieval, credential theft, concealment, cleanup and output return: none is present. Additional hostile traits would duplicate remote command execution or invent behavior. General CMD dataflow is limited; the existing YARA binds this unquoted file, variable and loop form.
